title: Finite torsion Tate twists are etale locally free lines
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $N\geq1$ be an integer invertible in every local ring of $T$, and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$. Work on the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], with constant sheaves $A_T$ and $(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], their module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $\mu_{N,T}$ be the sheaf of abelian groups $U\mapsto\{z\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times:z^N=1\}$, with its $\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z$-module action $a\cdot z=z^a$. Define $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N\mathbf Z)_T} A_T$, $A_T(0)=A_T$, and $A_T(r)=A_T(1)^{\otimes_{A_T}r}$ for $r\geq1$. Then for every $r\geq0$ there is an etale covering $\{T_i\to T\}$ with $A_T(r)|_{T_i}\cong A_{T_i}$ as module sheaves. In particular these sheaves are locally constant [def-constructible-locally-constant], locally free of rank one, and flat: tensoring with them preserves exact sequences of module sheaves.

proof.text: Cover $T$ by affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$. The integer $N$ is a unit in $R$: its local inverses exist by the local-ring hypothesis and agree on overlaps, so glue. Set $B=R[z]/(z^N-1)$ and $P=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Apply [lem-sbc-root-split-away-cover-etale] with $g=1,n=N$; its open $D(1)$ is all of $P$, so $P\to V$ is etale. Put $\Delta=\prod_{0\le a<b<N}(z^a-z^b)$ and $W=D(\Delta)\subset P$. For every point $t$ of $V$, choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of its residue field. Since $N$ is a unit, its characteristic does not divide $N$. By [lem-sc-primitive-root] choose a primitive $N$th root $\zeta\in\Omega$. The map $B\to\Omega$ sending $z$ to $\zeta$ defines a geometric point over $t$; its value on $\Delta$ is nonzero, so it lies in $W$. Thus both $P\to V$ and $W\to V$ are surjective. The inclusions $W\to P$ and $V\to T$ are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale]. To see that $W\to V$ is etale using exactly the covering-composition statement, compose the cover $\{P\to V\}$ with the cover $\{W\to P,\operatorname{id}_P\}$; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-composition] says each composite is etale. Now compose the affine-open cover of $T$ with the surjective etale maps $W\to V$ by the same lemma. These $W$ give an etale cover of $T$ with a unit $z$, $z^N=1$, and all differences $z^a-z^b$ invertible.

proof.text:
On one $W$ write $r_j=z^j$ for $0\le j<N$. The constant-presheaf homomorphism $a\mapsto z^a$ extends to $	heta:(\mathbf Z/N)_W	o\mu_{N,W}$ by the defining universal property of the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. We verify it is an isomorphism directly, without assuming that a set-sheaf trivialization preserves the group law. For any ring of sections over $W$, monic division gives $X^N-1=\prod_j(X-r_j)$: after division by the first $k$ factors, evaluate at the next $r_k$; the earlier differences are units, so the remaining quotient vanishes at $r_k$, permitting the next division. After $N$ divisions the quotient is the constant $1$. The Lagrange polynomials $L_j(X)=\prod_{k
e j}(X-r_k)/\prod_{k
e j}(r_j-r_k)$ satisfy $\sum_jL_j(X)=1$. Indeed the difference has degree less than $N$ and vanishes at all $r_j$; the same successive monic-division argument makes it zero. If $x^N=1$ is a section on an etale $U	o W$, set $e_j=L_j(x)$. Then $\sum_j e_j=1$ and $e_j(x-r_j)=(x^N-1)/\prod_{k
e j}(r_j-r_k)=0$. Hence the opens $D(e_j)$ cover $U$, and on $D(e_j)$, $x=r_j$. Thus every root is locally a power of $z$. If two constant residues $a
e b$ give equal powers on a nonempty object, the unit $r_a-r_b$ vanishes there, which is impossible. Locally represented sections of the constant sheaf therefore have equal image only when they agree locally. The local inverses just constructed are unique on overlaps and glue by the sheaf axiom; they give an inverse of $	heta$. Finally $z^{a+b}=z^az^b$ and $(z^a)^b=z^{ab}$ show that $	heta$ is an isomorphism of $(\mathbf Z/N)_W$-module sheaves.

proof.text: Restriction to an etale object is localization of [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]: for an object $U\to W$, its coverings and their intersections are exactly its coverings and intersections on $T$. Local section representatives and their local equality relations in sheafification are consequently identical on these two sites. In particular, sheafifying the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] gives $A_T|_W=A_W$ and $(\mathbf Z/N)_T|_W=(\mathbf Z/N)_W$; sheafifying the section tensor presheaf gives the restricted tensor product. By [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], tensoring the module isomorphism of step 2 with $A_W$ therefore identifies $A_T(1)|_W$ with $(\mathbf Z/N)_W\otimes_{(\mathbf Z/N)_W}A_W$. The multiplication map $b\otimes a\mapsto ba$ has inverse $a\mapsto1\otimes a$; the balancing relation gives $b\otimes a=1\otimes ba$. These are mutually inverse sheaf morphisms, so $A_T(1)|_W\cong A_W$. The scalar map $\mathbf Z/N\to A$ exists precisely because $NA=0$. No freeness or flatness of $A$ over $\mathbf Z/N$ is needed.

proof.text: The same covering works for every tensor power. For $r=0$ use the identity $A_T(0)|_W=A_W$. For $r=1$ use step 3. If $A_T(r)|_W\cong A_W$, the recursive tensor-power definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and multiplication $A_W\otimes_{A_W}A_W\cong A_W$ identify $A_T(r+1)|_W$ with $A_W$. This proves the induction for all $r\ge0$. The resulting cover is a trivialising datum in [def-constructible-locally-constant], so each twist is locally constant. On every $W$ its single generator is a basis over $A_W$, exactly the local-freeness-of-rank-one assertion.

proof.text: Fix $r$ and put $L=A_T(r)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift], every geometric point has a lift to one member $W$ of the cover in step 1. The stalk definition [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] gives the same stalk on $T$ and on the localized site at this pointed $W$: replace any pointed neighbourhood $U$ by $U\times_TW$ with its specified pair of lifts, a pointed refinement, and do the same for equalities of germs. These fibre products exist in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Thus the local basis of step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk] give $L_{\bar t}\cong A$, as $A$-modules since the germ comparison respects multiplication. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the forgetful functor from module sheaves to abelian sheaves is exact. For any short exact sequence $0\to F'\to F\to F''\to0$ of $A_T$-module sheaves, [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] gives a short exact sequence of underlying abelian stalks, with $A$-linear maps. By the natural tensor-stalk isomorphism in clause (1) of [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar], the stalk sequence after tensoring with $L$ identifies with the original sequence tensor $A$, hence with the original sequence via $m\otimes a\mapsto am$. Here the tensor over the constant ring sheaf agrees with the sheafification of tensors over $A$: locally each coefficient section is constant, so the balancing relations for a section of $A_T$ are locally exactly those for elements of $A$. Thus the cited comparison applies to precisely the tensor of the statement. Exact stalks imply exactness of the tensor sequence: its kernel at the first term, middle homology, and cokernel at the last term have zero stalks by exactness of the stalk functor; apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to their maps to the zero sheaf. They vanish. Tensoring with $L$ preserves short exact sequences, and hence exact sequences by factoring through images. This is the claimed flatness.
